article.headline: Games To Watch: Unbeaten starts collide at Tylertown and St. Patrick
article.html:
Unbeaten starts face their clearest test when they meet each other. Amite County visits Tylertown in boys basketball Tuesday, November 17, while Harrison Central travels to St. Patrick for a girls matchup between teams without a reported loss. On the soccer field, Oak Grove and Gulfport bring unbeaten records of their own into a meeting on the Coast.

Those matchups lead this selection of Mississippi varsity games to watch tonight. Basketball offers opportunities to protect perfect records or challenge a strong early start; soccer brings a pair of unbeaten opponents together and gives Oxford a chance to test Lewisburg. All listed start times are Central Standard Time.

Boys basketball: Amite County and Tylertown put perfect starts together

Amite County at Tylertown is scheduled for 7 p.m. The visiting Trojans enter at 4-0 and the Chiefs at 3-0, making this a direct test of two unbeaten openings. Neither team has a loss to explain away: a decisive result would give the winner another victory while handing the other its first defeat. The listing identifies this as a nonconference game, so the immediate significance is the strength of the start rather than district positioning.

Girls basketball: St. Patrick and Louisville defend unbeaten records

Harrison Central visits St. Patrick at 6 p.m. with the Red Rebels listed at 3-0 and the Fighting Irish at 6-0. St. Patrick has the longer unbeaten run, but Harrison Central arrives with a perfect record as well. That combination gives the matchup more substance than a routine early-season date: both sides can measure a clean opening against another team that has kept winning.

At the same time, Louisville’s girls visit Pontotoc at 6 p.m. The Wildcats bring a 6-0 record into a nonconference game against the 2-1 Warriors. Pontotoc has a winning start of its own and the home floor; Louisville has the opportunity to extend a longer winning run on the road. The contrast makes the game worth following without treating the teams’ different numbers of reported games as a complete measure of their strength.

Boys basketball: unbeaten visitors, unbeaten hosts and winning challengers

Meridian heads to Neshoba Central at 7 p.m. with a 4-0 record, while the Rockets are 4-1. This is a meeting of teams that have each already collected four wins, with Neshoba Central trying to turn home court into Meridian’s first setback. The Wildcats can preserve a perfect start against a host whose early record gives the matchup clear competitive interest.

Ripley’s boys visit Mooreville at 7 p.m. The Tigers are listed at 2-0 and the Troopers at 4-1. The matchup’s scoring-averages table lists Ripley at 70.5 points per game and Mooreville at 58.4. Those figures come from different early-season samples, but they give the matchup an offensive thread to follow: whether Ripley can maintain its reported pace against a host with more games behind its winning record.

In DeSoto County, Lewisburg visits Center Hill at 7:30 p.m. The Mustangs enter at 3-0 and the Patriots at 2-1. Center Hill can keep its perfect opening going at home, while Lewisburg has a chance to deliver a local opponent’s first defeat. Although the schools are county rivals, the current game listing identifies the contest as nonconference.

Boys soccer: unbeaten teams meet in Gulfport; Lewisburg faces Oxford

Oak Grove at Gulfport kicks off at 7 p.m. The Warriors are listed at 6-0-2 and the Admirals at 5-0-1. Both have avoided defeat, but both also have draws, so this is a test of unbeaten records rather than perfect ones. A winning result would separate the teams on the night and end the opponent’s loss-free opening; another draw would preserve both unbeaten marks.

Oxford visits Lewisburg at 7 p.m. The Patriots bring a 4-0 record, with the Chargers at 2-1-1. Lewisburg is trying to maintain a perfect opening, while Oxford offers a winning-record challenge that includes experience with both a defeat and a draw. The game gives the Patriots another chance to protect their home field and the Chargers an opportunity to interrupt an unbeaten start.

For recent background on teams in tonight’s selection, revisit our varsity recap featuring Meridian basketball and Lewisburg soccer.
